# Persisted artifact compatibility corpus

This corpus is generated by Zeppelin's real artifact builders and decoded by
`tests/artifact_fixture_tests.rs`. The comparator enumerates `src/format.rs::FORMATS`,
requires every registry family in every version directory, validates every
declared digest and size, and runs the typed production decoders where a codec
needs external shape information.

## Why this directory is not `v0.2.0`

`unreleased-936994f/` is a snapshot of the current, unreleased writer at git
commit `936994fedbc53a3e78bb7f7a5e44373b6e0ebcd1`. The crate still reports
`0.2.0`, but this writer is twelve commits past the `v0.2.0` tag: it writes IVF
bootstrap version 3 and ships an OpenAPI 0.2.1 contract. Naming these bytes
`v0.2.0` would falsely claim they were emitted by the released binary.
`MANIFEST.toml` records the full git commit, crate version, fixed generation
time, and `release_status = "unreleased current-format snapshot; not v0.2.0"`.

When the writer has a truthful release version, add a new immutable `vX.Y.Z/`
directory. Never rewrite an older release directory. Removing a legacy decoder
requires removing the fixture that exercises it in the same commit and
documenting that compatibility break in the changelog.

## Regeneration

From the repository root:

```bash
UPDATE_ARTIFACT_FIXTURES=1 cargo test --test artifact_fixture_tests generate_unreleased_936994f -- --exact
```

The generator uses `tests/common/vectors.rs::random_vectors` (seed 42), fixed
attributes, a fixed timestamp, explicit fragment/segment/branch ULIDs, the
fixed TwoBit sketch rotation seed, and seeded quantization/FDE transforms.
Hierarchical construction currently mints its root ULID internally, so the
generator decodes that real builder output and re-serializes it under the fixed
root ID `root_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAY`. `DeterministicDev` is enabled only
inside the generator's late-interaction path.

Run the command twice and compare the complete directory, including
`MANIFEST.toml`; a difference is a generator bug, not a reason to loosen a
test.

## Comparison policy

The following `checksum_input = true` registry families must decode and
re-encode byte-identically: `manifest` (current MessagePack only),
`wal_fragment`, `input_wal_fragment`, `ivf_bootstrap`,
`cluster_data_object`, `resident_sketch`, and `late_state_section`.

All other families are structure-compared with their registry probe and typed
decoder because the registry does not classify their encoding as a manifest
binding/checksum input. The legacy JSON manifest is also structure-compared:
the current manifest encoder intentionally emits MessagePack, so asking it to
reproduce the legacy `{` arm would test a different encoding. This distinction
does not permit generator flapping—the complete generated directory must still
be byte-identical across two runs.

Registry rows with no wire-version discriminator intentionally have a
future-version probe that returns an error; the comparator routes those rows to
their typed decoder rather than pretending they have a version header.

The semantic checks additionally pin cluster-zero's `tenant = "blue"` bitmap
to row position `[0]`, round-trip the late-state section, verify every
manifest-rooted query artifact is present, and run production strong queries.
The pinned results are ANN `vec_0, vec_5, vec_6` and BM25
`vec_0, vec_1, vec_2` for `zeppelin golden artifact`; they are duplicated in
`MANIFEST.toml` as corpus metadata.
